Builder S6d, 2026-09-24. Binding on every symbol in `app/assets/ox-sprite.svg`
and on anything that ever draws a glyph for this theme.

This document exists because two rounds of goal icons were rejected with the
same sentence: *"You are still using generic icon-library metaphors and then
adding small orange details."* The answer is not a taste note. It is a
construction language with numbers, taken off the mark itself, so that a
builder who has never seen the brand can redraw any symbol and it will belong.

It supersedes the drawing guidance in `docs/build/progress/S6a.md` §1.2–§1.4.
The architecture in S6a, symbol ids, `class="ox-sym"`, the `-s` twin rule, the
accent classes, `data-mirror`, is unchanged and is restated here so this file
stands alone.

---

## 0. The source

`public/assets/brand/optimalx-mark.svg`, one path, four filled parallelogram
arms, no curve anywhere:

```
M320.37 30 L459.23 30 L329.72 222 L205.71 222 L198.29 210.99 Z
M180.02 246 L287.37 246 L304.53 271.44 L173.3 466 L31.63 466 Z
M9.28 154  L141.45 154 L225.09 278 L92.92 278 Z
M273.21 198 L408.13 198 L502.56 338 L367.64 338 Z
```

Everything below is measured off that path (`docs/build/X-IDENTITY-2026-09-22.md`
§1 has the derivation and the rms residuals).

The rule the whole system turns on: **the mark is made of planes, not lines.**
Eight of its eighteen edges are horizontal and ten are at 34° from vertical.
Nothing is round, nothing is 45°, and every direction change happens on a
horizontal ledge. An icon family that only ever draws 2-unit outlines can never
look like it, however many orange slashes it carries.

---

## 1. The five rules

### R1, Two inks: the line and the plane

| ink | what it is | how it is drawn |
|---|---|---|
| **line** | a contour, a scale, a pulse, a rail | `stroke-width="2"` off the symbol, `stroke-linecap="square"`, `stroke-linejoin="miter"`, `stroke-miterlimit="4"` |
| **plane** | the mass of the symbol: a bolt, a needle, an arrowhead, a body, a hair lock | a closed `<path>` with **`fill="currentColor" stroke="none"`**, or the accent class, which is fill-only by definition |

A plane's narrow dimension is **4.5 units**, which is **22.5 % of the 20-unit
optical box**, the mark's own bar thickness (X-IDENTITY §1.5: mean
perpendicular thickness 113.50 of 493.28 wide = 23.0 %). A plane may run
**3.0–3.5 units** where two planes have to sit side by side (`goal-ideal-weight`)
and **2.4–2.8** for a needle or an arrowhead, and it may not go below 2.4, at
that point it is a line pretending to be a plane and the symbol reads thin.

`stroke="none"` on a mono plane is not optional. The symbol carries
`stroke-width="2"`, so a plane without it is painted one unit fat on every edge
and the 4.5 becomes 6.5.

**Every symbol that carries mass carries at least one plane.** A set of pure
outlines is the thing the owner rejected.

### R2, Two diagonals, and no others

`tan 34° = 0.675`. That is the only slope in the system, read two ways:

- **34° from vertical**, `dx = 0.675 · dy`. The mark's arms.
- **56° from vertical**, `dy = 0.675 · dx`. Its complement, the mark's other read.

With horizontal (`dy = 0`) and vertical (`dx = 0`) that is the whole lattice:
**0 / 34 / 56 / 90**. Tolerance is ±0.06°, which means a segment's `dx/dy` must
land inside `[0.6734, 0.6762]`, three decimals of coordinate, not two.

**45° is banned by name** and the test fails on it. Three universal glyphs are
named exceptions because 45° *is* their convention and the owner requires the
universal set to stay conventional: `ox-search` (the magnifier handle),
`ox-arrow` and `ox-external` (the arrowheads).

Curves are allowed **where the object has one**, a heart lobe, a gauge dial, a
body contour, a skull, a capsule end, a lens, a wheel. A curve is always
**closed by a straight lattice edge and a chamfer**, so the silhouette still
ends in hard corners. A curve is never used to soften a corner.

Practical note: author with `dy` on a 0.4 grid and `dx` falls on a 0.27 grid -
`dy 2 → dx 1.35`, `4 → 2.70`, `6 → 4.05`, `8 → 5.40`, `10 → 6.75`, `12 → 8.10`,
`14 → 9.45`. Those pairs are exactly 0.675 and need no rounding.

### R3, The chamfer

Where a corner would be square, it is **cut**, on the lattice, never rounded and
never bevelled at some convenient angle. The mark's NE arm cuts **14.86 of a
138.86-wide arm, 10.7 % of the plane's width**. Scaled to the 20-unit box that
is a cut of **2.6 units along the long side by 1.75 across** (2.6 × 0.675 =
1.755), which is the default chamfer.

- **Minimum 1.75 units.** A smaller cut is invisible at 24 px and is noise in
  the path data. If the corner cannot take 1.75, leave it square.
- **One chamfer per symbol, two at most.** It is a signature, not a texture.
- The chamfer sits on the part that reads as the symbol's **foot or tip** -
  the bottom of a heart, the end of a strand, the shoulder of a body, the foot
  of a tub, the strike end of a bolt.

### R4, Direction changes are hard, and the ledge has a ratio

A direction change is a **horizontal ledge**, never a curve and never a bevel.
The mark's channel jogs **83.78 px along a ledge 24 px tall, a ratio of 3.49**
(X-IDENTITY §1.5), and that is the mark's signature.

So: when a symbol steps sideways (the notch of a bolt, the offset of two arms,
the break of a band), the **run along the ledge is 3.49 × the vertical
separation of the two ledges**. `goal-energy` is the reference implementation:
ledges at y 10.27 and 13.73 (separation 3.46), runs of 12.08 (12.08 / 3.46 =
3.49).

### R5, One accent, and it is part of the object

The accent is painted **only** through a class, so the theme token drives it and
no literal colour ever appears in the sprite:

| class | resolves to | use |
|---|---|---|
| `ox-icon__accent` | `fill: var(--ox-icon-mono, var(--ox-accent))`, `stroke: none` | an accent **plane** |
| `ox-icon__accent ox-icon__accent--stroke` | `fill: none`, `stroke: var(--ox-accent)` | an accent **line** |

- **One accent element per symbol.** Never two, never a scatter.
- **10–15 % of the symbol's ink.** Ink = plane area + (line length × 2).
- It is the part that **moves, measures, pulses, targets, is active, or is the
  brand cut**: a pulse, a needle's redline, a strike tip, a measuring band, a
  wheel, a chip, a keyhole, a play triangle.
- It is **never** a floating diamond, a stray triangle, a decorative slash or a
  dot that is not part of the object. "Do not place a tiny orange slash inside
  every icon" is a standing instruction, and **a healthy share of the set stays
  pure monochrome**, the test floor is 30 %.
- The symbol must read **first in single-colour black or white**. Cover the
  accent: if the metaphor dies, the symbol is wrong.

---

## 2. The box

| rule | value |
|---|---|
| Grid | 24 × 24, `viewBox="0 0 24 24"` on every symbol |
| Optical box | **20 × 20**, every drawn point inside `[2, 22]` |
| Fill the box | the object reaches within 1.25 of the inset (≤ 3.25 / ≥ 20.75) on **at least two** sides |
| Elements | `<path>` only. No `<circle>`, `<rect>`, `<line>`, `<polygon>`, no `rx`/`ry`, no `transform` |
| Weight | `stroke-width="2"` as a **presentation attribute on the `<symbol>`** |
| Terminals | `stroke-linecap="square"`. Never `round`, never `butt` |
| Joins | `stroke-linejoin="miter"` with `stroke-miterlimit="4"` |
| Symbol fill | `fill="none"` on the `<symbol>`; planes declare their own fill on the path |

The weight lives on the symbol because `<use>` clones into a shadow tree that
inherits from the **`<use>` element**, not from the sprite root. A width on the
sprite's root `<svg>` never reaches a rendered path. That defect is what made
the first icon set look like hairlines (S6a §1.1).

The 16 px step takes a slightly fatter relative stroke, through an inherited
custom property, because a descendant selector cannot cross the `<use>`
boundary but a simple class selector can:

```css
.ox-sym{stroke-width:var(--ox-icon-stroke,2px)}
.ox-icon--16{--ox-icon-stroke:2.25px}
```

Both rules ship inlined in the sprite **and** in `_primitives.scss`.

---

## 3. Two optical variants

- **Standard** `#ox-{name}`, drawn for 24, 32, 36.
- **Simplified twin** `#ox-{name}-s`, drawn for 20 and 16. `Icon.tsx` rewrites
  the `href` when `size <= 20` **and** the twin exists.

A twin is **not a scaled copy**. It keeps the silhouette and loses parts: a
segment off a pulse, a ring off a tub, the outline off a star, a step off a
profile. Its counters are fatter and its accent is kept only where it still
reads at 16.

A name `Icon.tsx` simplifies with no `-s` in the sprite is a **broken `<use>`**
at 16 and 20, so the twin set and `OX_SIMPLIFIED_ICON_NAMES` are asserted equal.

---

## 4. RTL

Arabic is the default direction. **Brand geometry never flips.** Exactly five
symbols carry `data-mirror="1"` and are the only ones `Icon.tsx` mirrors:
`chevron-start`, `chevron-end`, `arrow`, `external`, `play`.

`chevron-down` and `chevron-up` are vertical and do not mirror. **`ox-mark`
never mirrors**, and neither does a chamfer, a tub foot, a strand tip or any
other brand cut.

---

## 5. The three families, and how the rules land on each

### 5.1 Product categories, frozen

`protein`, `creatine`, `pre-workout`, `amino-acids`, `omega-3`,
`vitamins-minerals`, `collagen-beauty`, `daily-health`, `snacks-bars`,
`accessories`.

The owner ruled on 2026-09-24: *"the icons in shop by category were fine, they
just got ruined."* These ten are kept **byte-for-byte** from git `3f952b3`.
They carry no `stroke-width` and no `class="ox-sym"`, deliberately: the width
was *inherited* before the redraw and it was not one number, 1 on the home
tiles, 1.25 on the categories index (`.ox-cat-card__icon`, `_b4-listing.scss`).
A presentation attribute on the symbol beats an inherited CSS value, so writing
*any* number onto these ten would silently change the categories index.

**They are exempt from this document.** They may not grow a twin, and they may
not be redrawn unless the owner says so. `tests/common/sprite.test.ts` names
them in `OWNER_APPROVED_ORIGINALS` and pins the allowlist, so a new symbol
cannot quietly join them.

`#ox-mark` is exempt too, on different grounds: it is the mark, single colour,
full bleed, pinned byte-for-byte by `scripts/check-identity.mjs` (rule
`mark-drift`).

### 5.2 Goals and benefits, the reference implementation

The six goal symbols are where the five rules were derived and are the worked
example any new symbol should be read against.

| symbol | plane | line | accent | the rule it demonstrates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `goal-energy` | the whole bolt |, | the 56° strike cut at the tip | **R4**, two 34° arms, two horizontal ledges, run/separation 3.49 |
| `goal-performance` | the needle, tapered on a 34° and a 56° edge, on a chamfered hub | the dial | the redline at the top of the scale | **R1**, a curve (the dial) closed by planes |
| `goal-general-health` | the whole heart |, | the pulse | **R3**, the foot cut by a 56° chamfer |
| `goal-recovery` | two arrowheads, each a 34° edge + a 56° edge + a horizontal back | two arcs | the pulse at the centre | **R2**, an arrowhead with no 45° anywhere in it |
| `goal-hair-skin` | the hair, with a chamfered strand tip | the profile: brow step, angular nose, lip, chin, jaw | the sparkle, whose eight edges alternate 34° and 56° | **R2**, curves used only where the object has one |
| `goal-ideal-weight` | the two body contours |, | the measuring band with its target notch | **R3**, the shoulder chamfer; **R1**, planes at 3.4 because two sit side by side |

The sparkle is worth naming as a reusable primitive. An eight-vertex star whose
edges alternate 34° and 56° exists for exactly one ratio: with outer radius `a`,
the inner vertices sit at `(±0.403a, ±0.403a)`. Nothing else on the lattice
closes.

### 5.3 Universal UI, conventional metaphors, brand construction

A magnifier is a circle and a handle. A cart is a basket on two wheels. A house
is a roof and a box. **The metaphor does not change.** What the system gives
these symbols is geometry, stroke, terminals and chamfer:

- diagonals move onto 34/56 (a chevron drawn at 50.6° is drawn at 56°);
- square corners that read as a foot take the chamfer;
- the accent, where there is one, is the working part (the cart's wheels, the
  play triangle, the lock's keyhole, the warning's bang) at 10–15 %;
- most of this family carries **no accent at all**, and that is the point.

### 5.4 Service and trust

Same contract as 5.3, with one extra: these symbols carry the store's promises
(shipping, authenticity, expiry, payment), so their accent is reserved for the
part that **certifies**, the check in a shield, the date on a calendar, the
chip on a card, the speed lines on a truck.

---

## 6. What a reviewer checks

In order. A symbol that fails an earlier line is not saved by a later one.

1. **Does it read in one glance, in black on white, at 24 px, with no label?**
   If not, nothing else matters.
2. Does it still read at **16 px** through its twin?
3. Is every straight edge on **0 / 34 / 56 / 90** (±0.06°), with **no 45°**?
4. Is every point inside **[2, 22]**, and does the object reach the inset on
   **≥ 2 sides**?
5. Is there **at least one plane**, at least 2.4 units across?
6. Is there **exactly one accent**, at **10–15 % of ink**, and is it a working
   part of the object?
7. Does the symbol carry `class="ox-sym"`, `fill="none"`, `stroke="currentColor"`,
   `stroke-width="2"`, `square`, `miter`, `miterlimit 4`?
8. Is there **no literal colour**, no `transform`, no primitive shape element?
9. Does it have a twin if `Icon.tsx` names it, and does it carry `data-mirror`
   only if it is one of the five directional glyphs?

Machine checks for 3, 4, 7 and 8 live in `tests/common/sprite.test.ts`. The
geometry audit that reports bounding box, ink, accent share and the angle set
per symbol is the script quoted in `docs/build/progress/S6d.md` §5.

---

## 7. Things that are forbidden, in one place

- 45° anywhere except `ox-search`, `ox-arrow`, `ox-external`.
- `stroke-linecap="round"`, `stroke-linejoin="round"`, `stroke-linejoin="bevel"`.
- `rx`, `ry`, `transform`, `<circle>`, `<rect>`, `<line>`, `<polygon>`,
  `<polyline>`.
- A literal colour, `#F15C22`, `#EE4D22` or any other, anywhere in the sprite.
- More than one accent element in a symbol.
- An accent that is not part of the object: a floating diamond, a corner
  triangle, a decorative slash, a dot with no job.
- A curve used to soften a corner.
- A plane without `stroke="none"`.
- A `stroke-width` on any symbol other than `2` (the ten frozen originals and
  `ox-mark` carry none at all, by design).
- Touching the ten product-category originals or `#ox-mark`.
- A hand-drawn `<path d="…">` anywhere in `app/**` outside `ox-sprite.svg`,
  `Icon.tsx` and the `PdpIcon.tsx` legacy shim.

---

## 8. A colour note the owner still has to settle

The reference sheets render the accent as **#F15C22**. The theme's live token
is `--ox-accent` → `--color-primary` → **#EE4D22** in `tokens.css`, which comes
from the Salla dashboard. The sprite hardcodes neither, so the icons take
whatever the token says, but the two oranges are not the same, and if #F15C22
is the intended brand colour that is a change to `--color-primary` in the
dashboard plus `tokens.css`, never a change to the sprite.
